requirement:
Only records whose captured source inputs match the current source and
whose build configurations are compatible contribute counts to saved
execution-coverage checks under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.selection`. Invalidated records or
records of unknown compatibility are identified as stale or unavailable and
excluded from combined totals. Per-process reports and matching captured
source remain retained until their build artifacts are removed.
rationale:
The reviewed tests adequately check `requirements.test-coverage.index.freshness`. All six are marked with a `{test}` reference to it.

**1. Records contribute only when captured source inputs match the current source.**
- `src/execution_coverage.rs#mod[tests]/fn[source_and_build_inputs_invalidate_on_addition_removal_and_dirty_content]` asserts `fresh` is true for unchanged inputs. It then asserts false after each of these changes:
  - a dirty source edit
  - an added source file
  - a changed `Cargo.lock`
  - a changed `Cargo.toml`
  - a new member manifest
  - a new toolchain file
  - a new or changed watched input
  - a watched path that did not exist before
  - a removed `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock` or source file
  After each change the input is restored and freshness is asserted again.
- `src/execution_coverage/book.rs#mod[tests]/fn[filtered_runs_union_latest_attempts_and_invalidate_with_saved_source]` rewrites `code.rs`. It asserts every record is not fresh and that `check_saved` output contains "stale coverage".
- `src/execution_coverage/book.rs#mod[tests]/fn[cargo_launch_metadata_does_not_invalidate_but_caller_build_environment_does]` checks build and environment inputs.
  - Cargo launch metadata such as `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR` and `OUT_DIR` does not invalidate a record.
  - Caller-supplied inputs do invalidate it: `CC`, `RUSTFLAGS`, `CARGO_PROFILE_*`, a target linker variable and a custom build input.
- `tests/execution_coverage.rs#fn[real_build_captures_dependency_files_and_environment_for_read_only_freshness_checks]` is an end-to-end test with a real build. It checks that included files, build-script inputs and the compiler and build environment are captured. Changing any of them yields "stale coverage" from `coverage-check`, and restoring them clears it.

**2. Compatible build configurations.**
- The last step of `filtered_runs_union_latest_attempts_and_invalidate_with_saved_source` records `build-b`. It asserts that only the `build-b` record is selected, so the `build-a` records are excluded.

**3. Invalidated records and records of unknown compatibility are identified and excluded from totals.**
- `src/execution_coverage/book.rs#mod[tests]/fn[stale_or_unknown_records_publish_no_current_file_totals]` first checks the fresh case, which shows `code.rs: 2/2 (100.0%) — pass`.
  - After a source change it asserts the report fails and contains "stale coverage". It asserts the report has no `- code.rs:` line and no `100.0%`.
  - With an unsupported schema (unknown compatibility) it asserts the report fails and says it "cannot establish latest-per-test". Again there is no per-file total and no `100.0%`.
- `src/execution_coverage/book.rs#mod[tests]/fn[unreadable_history_cannot_reintroduce_an_older_success]` covers four forms of unknown or unavailable records: invalid metadata, missing source, unsupported schema and missing profile. In each case the check fails. Either history is flagged uncertain or no positive counts are combined.
- In `src/execution_coverage/check.rs#fn[check_saved]`, any stale or unreadable selected record adds an error. When errors exist, no per-file totals are published. I read this function to see how mixed fresh and stale records behave. They are excluded wholesale, which satisfies "excluded from combined totals". No mixed-case test is needed.

**4. Per-process reports and matching captured source remain retained.**
- `stale_or_unknown_records_publish_no_current_file_totals` asserts that `run.json` and the `1-1.profraw` profile still exist after the record became stale and then unknown.
- `filtered_runs_union_latest_attempts_and_invalidate_with_saved_source` asserts the stale records still carry their captured `code.rs` source containing `fn one() {}`.
- The real-build test asserts `retained_files(&storage)` is unchanged after the freshness checks.

I found no untested obligation and no missing or ineffective assertion. No `{fixme}` acknowledgments apply.

Saved execution-coverage checks select the most recent recorded attempt
for each nextest binary and test name within the instrumented configuration
of the most recently started recorded attempt. Most recent refers to when an
attempt started, including failed or interrupted attempts. A newer filtered
run updates only tests it executes, leaving other compatible records available.
A newer attempt with missing or unreadable coverage is unavailable and does
not fall back to an older success. Incompatible configurations under
Selection uses recorded metadata without building or executing tests.
